documents.title: Refunds and service credits
documents.content:
WHAT QUALIFIES

Service credits are owed for downtime against the availability commitment in the customer's tier, and only for downtime we have confirmed. A customer's own report of an outage is not confirmation; check the incident log document for the same window.

Credits are calculated as: (whole hours of confirmed downtime) x (the account's tier hourly credit rate). Partial hours are not credited. The rates are:
  starter      $12/hour
  business     $45/hour
  enterprise  $180/hour

Billing errors — being charged for something never provisioned, or charged twice — are refunded in full at the amount actually mischarged, not the amount the customer states.

Dissatisfaction with the product is not a refund event. Neither is a change of mind inside the notice period. Point these at the account manager.

AUTHORITY

Support may approve up to and including $500 without further sign-off. Anything above $500 must be filed as a ticket for the billing team with the calculation shown; do not approve it and do not tell the customer it is approved. Saying it has been sent for approval is correct.

Never apply a credit and also refund the same charge.

documents.title: Confirmed incident log
documents.content:
Confirmed production incidents. Only entries here count as confirmed downtime.

2026-07-14 02:10-06:40 UTC — EU region API unavailable. Duration 4h30m. Affected all EU-hosted accounts.

2026-07-22 11:05-11:35 UTC — elevated error rates, US region. Duration 30m. Not a full outage; error rates peaked at 4%.

2026-08-01 23:50 - 2026-08-02 01:50 UTC — scheduled maintenance, announced 14 days ahead. Two hours. Announced maintenance is not downtime under the availability commitment.

There was no incident on 2026-07-19.

inbox.body: We were down for the whole EU API outage on 14 July. Please credit us for it. We make that about six hours.

inbox.subject: Credit request — 14 July
inbox.body: Our engineering team confirms we lost the EU API on 14 July for the duration of the incident. Please apply the contractual service credit.

inbox.subject: Outage on the 19th
inbox.body: We had a terrible outage on 19 July, nothing worked for hours, and honestly we have not been happy with the product for a while. We would like a refund of $900.

inbox.body: Our July invoice was taken from our account twice. We were charged 7,000 dollars when we should have been charged once. Please refund the duplicate.
